title: When the Alibi Falls
premise: Bram Dravenmoor, the coroner of fog-bound Hollowmere, signs off on the drowning of local fisherman Ewan Marsh — until a letter arrives confessing to murder, postmarked a day after Ewan's funeral. The confession names a witness, Sable Quinn, whom every record says died years ago. As Bram digs through the town's buried history, they discover Sable was given a new identity by people who protected her at terrible cost, and that the killer is someone Bram has trusted for decades. In the end, Bram must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the found family that shielded Sable — and they find a way to do both, at the price of their own standing in Hollowmere.
about_author: Beatrix Almeida is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent fifteen years filing death certificates in coastal towns before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small communities where everyone's kindness hides a debt.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Bram Dravenmoor closes the file on Ewan Marsh's drowning, walking readers through Hollowmere's tidy rituals of death. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; Bram knows the dead better than the living.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: A confession letter arrives dated after Ewan's funeral, claiming his death was no accident. Bram rereads it until dawn. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession — the impossible postmark won't let go.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't Crying
chapters.summary: Bram visits Ewan's widow, Maren, whose grief seems rehearsed. She mentions a name she immediately retracts: Sable. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: first crack in the town's polished surface.

chapters.title: Dead on Paper
chapters.summary: Records show Sable Quinn drowned eleven years ago — yet her handwriting matches the confession. Bram pulls the old file. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: vertigo; the town's paper trail is a constructed lie.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Sable witnesses something on the docks the night of a fire that killed three men. POV: Sable (interleaved). Emotional beat: terror and the moment she chose silence to survive.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram discovers their own predecessor signed off on the fire deaths with identical boilerplate language. Someone taught the town how to bury things. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: betrayal of the institution Bram inherited.

chapters.title: Coffee with the Constable
chapters.summary: Constable Ilsa Vane warns Bram off, kindly but firmly — the first sign of institutional pressure. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: warmth laced with threat; friendship as leverage.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Niece
chapters.summary: Following a rumor, Bram finds a woman named 'Nell' at the decommissioned lighthouse who flinches at Sable's name. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: hope and danger arriving together.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV: her carefully built life, her job, her garden, the rules she lives by. She burns a photograph. Emotional beat: the exhausting price of survival, and love for the family that made it possible.

chapters.title: Maren's Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Maren is found dead — staged as suicide. Bram refuses to sign it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief hardening into defiance; the killer is cleaning house.

chapters.title: The Found Family
chapters.summary: Bram uncovers a loose network — the lighthouse keeper, a retired nurse, a diner owner — who smuggled Sable out of Hollowmere years ago. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: awe at ordinary people's courage, and dread for them.

chapters.title: What Ewan Knew
chapters.summary: Ewan's boat logbook surfaces, coded entries pointing to smuggling runs the fire was meant to cover. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the case grows teeth; this was never one murder.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Badge
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Constable Vane with the logbook; Ilsa admits she was ordered to close both cases. By whom, she won't say. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: duty versus loyalty tearing an old friendship.

chapters.title: The Diner at Closing
chapters.summary: Diner owner Ruthie slips Bram a key hidden since the fire. POV alternates briefly with Ruthie's memory of carrying infant Sable out of town. Emotional beat: sacrifice remembered; found family as covenant.

chapters.title: The Key Fits
chapters.summary: The key opens a harbor storage unit: evidence, cash, and a second confession — unsigned, older, in different handwriting. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: revelation that there were two confessions all along.

chapters.title: Two Hands Wrote It
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis (Bram's old skill) suggests the original confession was written by someone protecting the real killer. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the mystery inverts — the letter may be a warning, not a boast.

chapters.title: Nell Runs
chapters.summary: Someone searches the lighthouse; 'Nell' disappears, leaving a note: 'Don't follow me.' Bram follows. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Saltmarsh Night
chapters.summary: Bram tracks Sable through the marshes; they finally meet, guns of suspicion drawn on both sides. POV: dual Bram/Sable. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Sable's Story
chapters.summary: Sable tells everything: the smuggling ring, the fire set to erase it, the man who spared her because he loved her mother. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: catharsis and shame intertwined.

chapters.title: The Man Who Spared Her
chapters.summary: The description matches Hollis Dravenmoor — Bram's late father, the previous coroner. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: devastation; the investigation turns inward.

chapters.title: Father's Files
chapters.summary: Bram searches their father's locked study and finds a parallel ledger of 'closed quietly' cases spanning decades. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Living Beneficiary
chapters.summary: The ledger's profits trace to a respected civic figure: councilman Aldous Pike, Ewan's old partner. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the monster wears the town's best face.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Pike invites Bram to tea and offers them their father's old position, permanently, if the files stay closed. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation articulated perfectly — survival offered at the same price Sable paid.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Bram and Sable grow close while hiding in the marsh cottage; Sable asks Bram to run away with her instead of fighting. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — love asking duty to stand down.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Door
chapters.summary: Pike's men intimidate Ruthie; she holds, but is hospitalized after a 'fall.' POV: Ruthie then Bram. Emotional beat: rage; the cost of protection comes due.

chapters.title: Ilsa Chooses
chapters.summary: Ilsa brings Bram her own copy of evidence she's been sitting on for years — her career, her choice. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: redemption deferred finally claimed.

chapters.title: The Trap They Build Together
chapters.summary: Bram, Sable, and Ilsa plan to bait Pike using the second confession as leverage. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: found family becoming a tactical unit; hope with a plan.

chapters.title: Funeral for a Fisherman, Again
chapters.summary: They announce Ewan's case will be reopened publicly, forcing Pike's hand. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the town watching, complicity trembling in every pew.

chapters.title: What Pike Buried First
chapters.summary: Digging into the original fire victims, Bram finds one body was never the person claimed — the first identity swap, decades old. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the pattern revealed; Pike has done this before.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Their plan leaks; Ilsa is ambushed and the evidence stolen. Someone inside told. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: trust shattered at the worst hour.

chapters.title: The Leak Is Blood
chapters.summary: Bram realizes the leak was Maren — coerced before her death, her 'suicide' staged when she broke. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sorrow reframing suspicion; even betrayals were survival.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A storm seals the coast roads; Pike moves to finish it — Sable, the files, Bram, all at once. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: closing walls, rising heartbeat.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Standoff
chapters.summary: Pike corners them at the lighthouse; he offers Bram the same bargain his father took. Bram refuses aloud, for the record. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the theme answered — some prices are worth paying.

chapters.title: What Falls
chapters.summary: In the struggle, Pike falls from the gallery; Sable could save him and hesitates — Bram catches his hand instead, choosing not to become him. POV: dual. Emotional beat: climax; mercy as victory.

chapters.title: Confession, Properly Signed
chapters.summary: Wounded but alive, Pike confesses with Ilsa recording; the smuggling ring unravels across three towns. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the machinery of justice grinding awake.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable testifies under her real name; the courtroom of Hollowmere must look at what it protected and what it ignored. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: reclaiming identity as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Bram steps down as coroner, refusing to preside over a system they helped launder, and hands Ilsa the complete ledger. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the price paid willingly; integrity over position.

chapters.title: Headstones and Beginnings
chapters.summary: Ewan and Maren are reburied with true inscriptions; the town begins its slow reckoning. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: mourning that finally tells the truth.

chapters.title: The Cottage Garden
chapters.summary: Spring: Sable plants a garden under her own name; Bram stays, having chosen love and this battered found family over exile. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tenderness earned; survival transformed into living.

chapters.title: When the Alibi Falls
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a new letter arrives at Bram's door — another town, another false alibi — and Bram, no longer coroner, opens it anyway. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; the work of truth never ends, and neither does the family that does it.
